meta.notes: Contradiction searches: 'sync works fine'/buffers, native TikTok/Marketplace Connect real-time claims, and vendor real-time claims. Amazon Seller Central help (cancellation rate), Capterra, linnworks.com, unicommerce.com, ProductHunt and most job boards were unfetchable, so Amazon's 2.5% threshold is cited from a seller-education publisher (SalesDuo). Reddit is cited via an archived snapshot. Prevalence figures (Nventory survey, Sumtracker case study) are vendor-published. No independent data on oversell frequency per peak or dollar cost per oversell; no merchant states a required latency. Prospects: 22 US Shopify merchants found via store names printed next to their reviews of Shopify-TikTok Shop / Amazon / marketplace sync apps on the Shopify App Store (reviews attributed by page order: store info follows its review), located via their own contact/about pages. Four use Marketplace Connect (eBay/Amazon/Walmart) rather than TikTok/Amazon-specific apps. Headcount verified only for Bjorem Speech; MERIT Beauty is likely above the SMB band; Tampon Tribe and RivaMira state only 'US'. Contacts only where the company's own page names an owner/founder (3). India ICP not prospected.

summary.statement: Merchants publicly describe repeated oversells when sync lags or fails: a Shopify+Amazon seller overselling because Shopify did not update fast enough, 3 single-unit oversells in one week, Amazon oversells lasting over a month.

Vendor-published figures suggest oversells are common (a Sumtracker case study at 5-7 incidents a month before sync; an Nventory survey claiming all 200 multichannel sellers asked had oversold within 90 days), but these come from sellers of sync software.
Webgility's survey of 800 sellers puts stock issues including overselling among the top challenges for 38%.
No independent source gives an oversell rate per order or per peak event; frequency remains anecdotal.

Marketplace penalties are concrete: Amazon's seller-fulfilled cancellation threshold is 2.5% over 7 days (2 cancellations at 80 orders a week) and offers may be deactivated above it; out-of-stock cancellations always count.
TikTok Shop counts out-of-stock cancellations as seller-fault cancellations that can bring enforcement, violation points and lost Account Health points.
In India, Amazon charges a 10% cancellation fee (orders under ₹10,000) and Flipkart ₹60 per seller-cancelled shipment since August 2026.
Merchants report a past Amazon suspension and a looming second one from oversell cancellations, customer refunds, a feared loss of a 20-year eBay store, and money lost to sync errors.
No source quantifies a typical dollar loss per oversell for a small merchant.
Merchants use native connectors (Shopify Marketplace Connect, the TikTok Shop channel) or third-party apps (Sellbrite, QuickSync, CedCommerce, CS Amazon Sync, Sumtracker, Syncio).

Reported shortcomings are batch intervals on cheaper tiers (Sellbrite free plan every 2 hours, first paid tier every 15 minutes) and, more often, silent failures: apps stop syncing without alerts, drop SKUs, or mishandle preorders.
Reliability rather than latency is the dominant complaint in reviews, and several vendors already advertise real-time or within-seconds sync.

In small Shopify brands the owners install and review the sync apps themselves; a larger brand hired an e-commerce operations specialist to resolve inventory sync issues across Shopify, TikTok Shop and its 3PL.
No evidence shows who signs off on the purchase in larger organisations.
Common mitigations are per-channel safety buffers, manual weekly diffs of inventory exports by SKU, and daily manual checks that the sync app is still running.
Buffers do not fix wrong source stock, and manual checking does not scale to hundreds or thousands of listings.
Accuracy matters most where marketplace thresholds are tight: on Amazon, two seller cancellations in an 80-order week reach the 2.5% limit.
A sync vendor concedes small stores on only Shopify and TikTok Shop may rely on native integrations at first, so urgency likely rises with volume and channel count.
No merchant states a required latency (seconds vs minutes) in their own words.
Switching triggers in the evidence are price jumps (Linnworks to £150-£450/month for sellers who only need quantity sync) and unreliable sync with slow support.
Merchants already pay in the hypothesis range: Sellbrite from $29/month, Syncio $19/$49/$99 by order volume, Sumtracker from $59/month, Marketplace Connect capped at $99/month.
Many low-cost apps already claim real-time sync, so a new entrant would have to win on verifiable reliability rather than speed alone.

current_solutions.statement: Most merchants rely on a native connector or a $19-$99/month sync app, and many vendors already claim real-time sync.
Merchants backstop the apps with safety buffers and manual SKU-level checks.
Larger brands hire operations staff to resolve sync issues during TikTok Live peaks.
